topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I tried to act casual, like it didn’t matter, asking about mutual friends and old times, but the more we talked, the clearer it became. He laughed at the stories I shared, nodding along, but his eyes gave him away. There was nothing there, no spark of recognition, no flicker of shared history. I kept the conversation light, steering it away from anything too personal, too loaded. It’s strange how you can sit across from someone, smiling and nodding, while inside you’re piecing together the ruins of something you didn’t know could still hurt this much. I wondered if I should have stayed away, if this was how things were now, just polite small talk and hollow smiles.
